title: Cigar-box fiddles and rattlesnake rattles inside them
summary: Frontier fiddles were made from cigar boxes and cedar necks with dried rattlesnake rattles dropped inside for loudness; he sold rattles for 25 cents.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up a first guitar or banjo, self-taught

blocks.x: Yeah. Well, now, I'll tell you what else you told me that was terribly interesting. I said to you, "Where did he get his first instrument from?" What did you tell me?
He'd go downtown and buy him a cigar -- no, he wouldn't buy it. He'd go down and get an old cigar box and that's the way they made the fiddles.
Yeah, but you told me that they cut them out of the trees.
No, that's for the neck.
Oh, I see what you mean. I couldn't understand that. Oh, yeah, they get the cigar box, yeah --

(Inaudible) cut it out and make that hole and then they make the hold up in there like a fiddle -- they cut it in the shape of a fiddle -- and they make in it, cut it out with a good sharp knife or anything and they would --
Yeah, but if they make it the shape of a fiddle, what do they do with the sides?
The sides?
Yeah.
They just cut a little bit out of the side and put (inaudible).
Yeah, but what I mean is this. It's how thick? An inch and a half thick?
What, the --
The cigar box or the fiddle.
(Inaudible) the same width as the fiddle (inaudible).
Yeah, but if you cut out the cigar box, you've got open sides, haven't you?
Yeah, they'd fill that in.
They'd fill it in. What with?
I dont' know.
Something. Plywood or something.
Yeah, maybe they'd -- they had ways they could wet that stuff and bend it and they'd dry the fiddle out and they'd seal it.
Well, I'll be darned.

And a lot of fiddles were made out of cigar boxes today, I guess, and they put a seam in the middle of them and some good ones ain't got no seam. And then we'd go out -- and then he'd go out and kill him a rattlesnake. If he was 20 year s old, you'd have ten rattles -- no, if he was ten years old, he'd have 20 rattles. Then he'd kill a rattlesnake and he'd get the rattles and he'd bring them back and they'd dry those rattles for about four days. When they dry out, then they drop them down in the fiddle. When you hit the fiddle, boy,them rattles would sound -- that fiddle would sound like an amplifier.
(Laughter.)
It would what? Resound, you mean?
Yeah, if you put the rattles in it, the rattlesnake rattles. But you dry them out and put the rattles in it.
And do you get a vibrating sound or what kind of sound?
No, you just get a loud sound with that wood, you can hear little rattles.
You mean you fill it with the rattles?
Yeah, you put them inside the fiddle.
Do they about fill it up?
No, you would only put just about ten rattles in there, one set.
Is that right?

Because they come by sets and you just dry it out and you just drop them in there when they dry and then that gives the sound on that and I imagine it would be the same thing with acoustic guitar. So then -- and all the fiddle players would use it and I was a good shot, so I'd go out and get me about -- kill me about five or six rattlers, shoot them, then I cut the tail off and bring the rattle in and dry them out and you'd get 25 cents a rattle from downtown. They'd sell them to fiddle players.
